question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Event on the road to the Carnatic Wars — its description and geographical context]
options: Assassination of Nawab Safdar Ali (1742) — created a power vacuum in Arcot, prompting Nizam-ul-Mulk's intervention in the Carnatic
Appointment of Anwar-ud-din (1744) — Nizam-ul-Mulk appointed him Nawab of Carnatic, displacing the popular Nawayat dynasty
Arrival of Dupleix as Governor of Pondicherry (1742) — Dupleix began fortifying Pondicherry and seeking alliances with local rulers
Capture of Madras by Nawab Anwar-ud-din (1745) — the Nawab captured Fort St. George from the British to enforce neutrality in his territories
wrong_fact: Nawab Anwar-ud-din did NOT capture Madras from the British in 1745. In 1745, Anwar-ud-din demanded that both the British and French maintain peace in his territory. The British initially respected this, but in 1746 the French under La Bourdonnais and Dupleix captured Madras from the British (Battle of Madras). Anwar-ud-din then sent his army to reclaim Madras from the French, which led to the Battle of Adyar (St. Thome) in October 1746.
explanation: Madras was captured by the French in 1746, not by the Nawab in 1745. The Nawab had demanded neutrality, but the French violated it. This prompted the Nawab to send his army under his son Mahfuz Khan, who was defeated by a small French force at the Battle of Adyar. Safdar Ali's murder in 1742 indeed destabilized the Carnatic, leading the Nizam to appoint Anwar-ud-din, which alienated the relatives of the former Nawab (including Chanda Sahib). Dupleix's arrival in 1742 marked the beginning of active French political intervention.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Battle / Military confrontation — its key details and historical outcome]
options: Battle of Adyar (St. Thome) (1746) — French forces defeated the much larger army of Nawab Anwar-ud-din, proving the superiority of disciplined, European-trained troops
Siege of Pondicherry (1748) — British fleet under Admiral Boscawen besieged Pondicherry by land and sea but failed to capture it before the monsoon set in
Battle of Ambur (1749) — Muzaffar Jung and Chanda Sahib, assisted by French troops, defeated and killed Nawab Anwar-ud-din, starting the Second Carnatic War
Battle of Swally (1612) — fought near Pondicherry, where the French navy defeated the Portuguese to secure their first factory site
wrong_fact: The Battle of Swally (1612) was NOT fought near Pondicherry, nor did the French participate. The Battle of Swally (Suvali) was fought off the coast of Surat (Gujarat) on the west coast of India. It was a naval battle between the English East India Company and the Portuguese, which paved the way for the establishment of the first English factory in Surat. The French East India Company was not even founded until 1664.
explanation: The Battle of Swally was an English-Portuguese naval clash near Surat in 1612, unrelated to Pondicherry or the French. The Battle of Adyar (1746) was a watershed moment where a small French force under Paradis defeated Nawab's army of 10,000 men under Mahfuz Khan, demonstrating the power of European military discipline. The British siege of Pondicherry (1748) under Admiral Edward Boscawen was successfully repulsed by Dupleix. The Battle of Ambur (August 1749) resulted in the death of Anwar-ud-din and placed Chanda Sahib on the throne of Arcot.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Geographical movement / event — strategic backdrop of the First Carnatic War]
options: British fleet under Commodore Barnett captures French merchant ships (1745) — took place in the Bay of Bengal, provoking Dupleix to call for naval support from Mauritius
La Bourdonnais' naval expedition from Isle de France (Mauritius) — sailed through the Maldives and anchored at Pondicherry, evading the British fleet to relieve the French
Nawab Anwar-ud-din's prohibition of hostilites — issued from Arcot to both Madras and Pondicherry, declaring that no European conflict would be permitted on his land
Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle negotiations — took place in the Netherlands, leading to the exchange of Madras for Pondicherry, which the British had captured in 1748
wrong_fact: The British did NOT capture Pondicherry in 1748, so it was not exchanged for Madras. The British siege of Pondicherry in 1748 under Boscawen was a failure, and Pondicherry remained under French control. Under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748), Madras (which the French HAD captured in 1746) was returned to the British in exchange for Louisbourg in North America (which the British had captured from the French).
explanation: The exchange at Aix-la-Chapelle was Madras (returned to Britain) for Louisbourg (returned to France). Pondicherry was never captured by the British during the First Carnatic War (Boscawen's siege failed). The other events are historically accurate: Barnett's capture of French ships in the Bay of Bengal in 1745 initiated hostilities; La Bourdonnais brought a French fleet from Mauritius to support Dupleix; and Nawab Anwar-ud-din issued orders from Arcot forbidding the companies from fighting in his territory, though Dupleix later ignored this to capture Madras.
